messages.subject: How to interpret histogram of CpG coverage?
parts:
Hello,
I'm working with targeted bisulfite sequencing data for the first time, and therefore I am not sure how to interpret the CpG coverage histograms.
The histogram from the methylKit tutorial has a peak on the left side with frequency values around 500 and on the right side (above around 1,75 log10 of read coverage per base) the boxes are very low (frquencies from 0.2 to 4.8). Here the histogram:


But my histograms are different! They look like this:

As I understood they should not have a second peak on the right side, right? And whats about the high log10 values. They should be around 2 and not until 4.5, right?

What can I conclude from such a histogram?

Can I use this data or is there a bias? If there is a bias, how can I handle this?


Here is a second one with the same problem:

Please help me with the interpretation. I'm thankful for every help. :-)

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] How to interpret histogram of CpG coverage?
parts:
targeted sequencing might produce such histograms. Basically, you have many CpGs that are covered with 1000 reads. I would say try to remove PCR bias you can try samtools or bismark has an option to do that, and carry on with the rest of the analysis. If there is some sort of validation you can do to prove yourself that methylation values you get from targeted sequencing is similar to another method, you can try to do that as well.

Best,
Altuna
